s01.setup: The ferry with the lamp oil has stalled at the dock. Passengers are waiting.
s01.line: That engine has not run so well in years.
s01.lit: The oil is ashore. The harbour lamp catches.

o.R: Repair the ferry engine with a toolkit
o.I: Examine a fuel sample to find why it stalled
o.A: Sketch a cheerful poster to explain the delay
o.S: Help older passengers find shade and a seat

s02.setup: The stone bridge's arch is cracked. A repair crew waits; lamp-bearers cross by midnight.
s02.line: My father laid that arch. Good to see it lit.
s02.lit: The lamp-bearers cross. The old arch glows.

o.R: Bolt steel supports under the cracked arch
o.I: Measure the cracks to find out why they formed
o.A: Design glowing signs to guide lamp-bearers across safely
o.E: Take charge of the repair crew and rally them

s03.setup: The tower clock that tells the lane when to light lamps is wrong.
s03.line: Right on dusk, and the whole lane is ready.
s03.lit: The tower strikes dusk. Every window lights at once.

o.R: Take apart the tower clock and mend its gears
o.I: Compare the chimes with sunset times for a pattern
o.A: Design a sundial for the lane to read dusk
o.C: Devise a lamp rota so lights come on smoothly

s04.setup: Apples are ripening faster than the village can press them. The press keeps jamming.
s04.line: Great juice, and the lamp is lit. Nice work.
s04.lit: The orchard is quiet. Its lamp swings among the trees.

o.R: Mend the juice press so it runs smoothly
o.I: Time each pressing run to find the bottleneck
o.S: Teach neighbours to run the press safely
o.E: Sell the extra apples to travellers on the road

s05.setup: Fog covers the mountain pass, the signal lamp is dim, and travellers keep arriving.
s05.line: Nobody was left behind in my pass tonight.
s05.lit: A thin gold line cuts the fog. The way is clear.

o.R: Climb the ridge and repair the signal lamp
o.I: Work out the safest route from weather readings
o.S: Chat with travellers and keep their spirits up
o.C: Set up check-ins so no traveller gets lost

s06.setup: Your borrowed stall opens soon. A strange old machine sits among piles of stock.
s06.line: A lit lamp is the best sign a stall can have.
s06.lit: The bazaar glows. A lamp hangs over your stall.

o.R: Get the old machine running with spanners and oil
o.I: Study which stalls draw crowds and learn why
o.E: Call out to shoppers and make your first sale
o.C: Arrange the stock so items are easy to find

s07.setup: A wide river blocks the road. Tired lamp-bearers rest by driftwood and a campfire.
s07.line: Your lamp's light will float all the way to the sea.
s07.lit: The group is rested. The lamp's glow drifts downstream.

o.R: Lash driftwood logs together into a raft
o.A: Paint a bright flag to mark the crossing point
o.S: Swap stories with the tired lamp-bearers by the fire
o.E: Rally the camp to pick a crossing plan

s08.setup: Market day is near. The power loom creaks, and a new weaver waits to learn.
s08.line: Every banner in town will glow brighter tomorrow.
s08.lit: Banners hang over the street. A lamp glows behind them.

o.R: Rebuild the loom's motor and hear it whirr
o.A: Invent a banner pattern for the loom to weave
o.S: Help the new weaver learn the loom
o.C: Set the weaving order so banners finish on time

s09.setup: A group must climb the glowing cliff before evening. Ropes and bolts are laid out.
s09.line: From up here the road looks like a string of stars.
s09.lit: The highest lamp is lit. The cliffs shine for miles.

o.R: Set anchor bolts into the rock for the route
o.A: Film the climb live for the village below
o.E: Inspire the group to push for the top
o.C: Time the rest stops so the team arrives fresh

s10.setup: A salt cart has a broken wheel, two traders argue, and a long queue grows.
s10.line: Quiet market, warm lamp. The best kind of night.
s10.lit: The market hums. Its lamp glows above the stalls.

o.R: Hammer a new wheel together for the salt cart
o.S: Keep the crowd calm with water and friendly talk
o.E: Strike a deal both traders will shake on
o.C: Speed up the queue with a better serving system

s11.setup: A clear night is coming. Visitors climb the hill to use the telescope.
s11.line: The sky has been waiting for this.
s11.lit: The hill lamp lifts its light, and the sky answers.

o.I: Track a planet's path through the telescope each hour
o.A: Photograph the night sky and edit the best shots
o.S: Help visitors find a comfy spot to watch
o.E: Start a stargazing club and sign up members

s12.setup: The lamp-herb garden is overgrown, the season is turning, and neighbours want herbs.
s12.lit: The garden is tidy. The lamp smells of rain and mint.

o.I: Test the soil to find which herbs grow best
o.A: Design a picture guide to the lamp-herbs for neighbours
o.S: Guide neighbours in growing herbs in pots at home
o.C: Rearrange the beds so one watering round reaches all

s13.setup: An old printing press was found in a cellar. Everyone wants to print something.
s13.line: Ink and light. They go together.
s13.lit: Paper fills the quarter. A lamp glows above the cellar door.

o.I: Work out how the old press works
o.A: Write the lead story for the first printed sheet
o.E: Sell the first printed sheets on the street
o.C: Line up print jobs so the press stays busy

s14.setup: Travellers rest here tonight. Several are unwell, and the medicine shelves run low.
s14.line: Steady light. They can rest now.
s14.lit: The house is calm. A steady lamp burns in the window.

o.I: Look for what the unwell travellers have in common
o.S: Bring warm drinks and blankets to unwell travellers
o.E: Take the lead and decide how the night runs
o.C: Rework the medicine shelves so urgent items come first

s15.setup: The bare festival square needs lanterns, a match, stalls and acts before dusk.
s15.line: All the lamps are lit. Let the festival begin!
s15.lit: The square is ready. Its lamp glows over the stones.

o.A: Decorate the bare square with lanterns and bunting
o.S: Coach the junior team for the festival match
o.E: Talk traders into taking stalls around the square
o.C: Plan the festival schedule so it runs on time

ila.1: Everyone said I'd take her place. I never chose it. I need to ask her why.
ila.6: Each keeper remembers her at a different job. Why would she try them all?

meta.premise: The lighthouse is dark. Find out why.
meta.outro: The lighthouse is lit. This is the light you carry.

sharpen.line: More lamps make your road clearer. Stop any time.

2.text: She worked beside me for a night. Then she went on.

4.text: She did my work here last night. She is close.

5.text: She tried my work for a day. She tried every kind.

7.text: I know where she went: the lighthouse. I promised to wait until you were ready.

screens.text: The door is open. The lamp is dark. A letter lies beside it.

I put this light out myself, so you could light it. A lamp I lit would only show my road. I took no oil, because the oil is yours to spend. I tried every kind of work so you could find yours. People will tell you what to be. The road was never mine. Choose yours.

R: You like getting your hands dirty.
Tools, wood, and a job done.
You like to fix things. Noted.
I: You look closely before you act.
Puzzles light you up. Jyo noticed.
A: A new shape, a new colour.
Your own touch on the town.
You made something that was not there.
That looks like you. Jyo glows.
S: You went to the people first.
Someone feels better because of you.
People matter to you. Jyo hums.
E: You saw a chance and took it.
C: You like things careful and steady.
You made it tidy and clear.
You like to keep order. Jyo approves.
mix: A little of both. That's fine.
Two kinds of work. No wrong answer.

meta.outroSharp: The lighthouse is lit, and your road is clearer. This is the light you carry.
